title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Kress named interim chief
h1: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's chief executive, and the stock has closed below a $4 trillion market value
description: Nvidia said on November 12, 2026 that Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and director. CFO Colette Kress is interim chief. Shares fell 12.75% for the week.
standfirst: He left immediately, four days after the board opened an investigation. Nvidia named its first board chair and will report quarterly results on Tuesday as planned.
keywords: Jensen Huang resigns, Nvidia CEO, Colette Kress interim CEO, Harvey Jones Nvidia chair, Nvidia stock $4 trillion, Nvidia earnings November 17 2026
takeaways: Nvidia announced on Thursday, November 12 that Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is interim CEO. Harvey C. Jones became the company's first board chair.
Shares fell 12.75% for the week. Third-quarter results are due Tuesday, November 17.
body: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's president, chief executive and a member of the board, effective immediately. The company announced the change on Thursday, November 12, in a statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, agreed to serve as interim CEO and will keep her finance role until a permanent successor is named. The board said it has begun a search and will consider internal and external candidates. It also appointed Harvey C. Jones as Nvidia's first-ever chair of the board.

"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team," Jones said in the statement. Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 after finance roles at companies including Cisco and Microsoft, according to the filing.

The company's statement gives no reason. The resignation came four days after the board opened an investigation following reports that Huang had a relationship with a Chinese woman believed to be a spy for Beijing. Huang disclosed an affair in a note to employees on Sunday, and news outlets reported further relationships later in the week, CNBC reported. Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on the latest report.

Shares closed about 4% lower on Thursday and fell another 2.01% on Friday, leaving Nvidia's market value below $4 trillion at the close for the first time since July 2025, according to CNBC. The stock lost 12.75% over the week. It was the sixth weekly decline in a row, the longest such run since 2012.
Before the resignation, several Wall Street analysts told CNBC that Huang's departure could cost the company as much as 20% of its market value.

Nvidia said it will report results for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 on Tuesday, November 17, at about 1:20 p.m. Pacific time, as previously scheduled, with a conference call at 2 p.m. The company gave no timeline for choosing a permanent chief executive.
